children: US stocks started the day on a weak note, with investors weighing geopolitical risks from the America-Iran conflict and renewed trade friction between Washington and Ottawa. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 611 points, or 1.1%, while the S&P 500 declined 0.5%. The Nasdaq Composite also slipped 0.5%.

Oil prices rose to a six-week high for a third straight session after Iran and the US exchanged strikes over the weekend. Brent crude oil futures climbed 2.3% to $99.22 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate futures rose 3.3% to $94.54.

Yemen's Tehran-backed Houthis attacked four cities in the south of US ally Saudi Arabia on Tuesday, wounding more than 70 people and setting oil installations ablaze in what appeared to be a major expansion of the six-month-old Middle East war. NASA satellite images showed a thick cloud of black smoke over the Jazan refinery and a column of white smoke rising from an oil distribution centre in Abha.
The benchmark 10-year Treasury note yield last week climbed to its highest level since November 2023, while the shorter-term 2-year note yield scaled to a January 2025 high.

Coal production has started recovering after a monsoon-related slowdown, with Coal Minister G Kishan Reddy saying output is expected to increase further if rainfall remains subdued in coal-producing regions. Reddy said 123.7 million tonnes (MT) of coal is currently available, enough to meet around 51 days of consumption at the rate of 2.4 MT a day. He said power generation companies and thermal power plants are not facing any shortage of coal.

title: Market Pulse: Key triggers to watch before the September 9 trading session
